channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Wildlife 2027 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: Printed photography exhibition on wildlife at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography, 4 to 28 February 2027 - a theme the gallery says has not had its own dedicated exhibition there before. The brief asks for "the visual delight of wildlife and the stories that they tell", in natural habitats or the unusual places animals turn up, and it also invites work on wildlife's relationships with humans, "both positive and negative", from the exotic to the domestic and the rural to the urban. Submission is free; photographers selected pay a £50 participation fee (a discount is offered to anyone selected for both of the gallery's February exhibitions, this and Golden Hour 2027), which covers printing at 16x12, 18x12 or 12x12 inches in gallery-owned frames. Selected participants have their work printed and hung in the gallery, shown in an online gallery on the website and included in an exhibition catalogue, receive a digital certificate of participation, have photos and video of the installed work shared on the gallery's social media, and are automatically put forward for its Photographer of the Month. Submit 1 to 8 JPEGs at 300ppi and at least 3,000 pixels on the shortest side, named Firstname-Surname, in one batch via Smash, WeTransfer or Dropbox to the gallery's submissions address, stating which exhibition you are entering, your nationality or country of residence and any links. Deadline 9 October 2026; acceptance notification by 14 October (only selected photographers are notified) and payment due by 28 October. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: Free (£50 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Golden Hour 2027 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: Printed photography exhibition at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography, 4 to 28 February 2027, on the golden hour - the gallery's brief describes it as "the period of time in the day just after sunrise or just before sunset when an array of amazing colours can be captured", and asks for work that explores the world through the colour, light, shadow, texture and shape that light makes possible. Submission is free; photographers selected pay a £50 participation fee (a discount is offered to anyone selected for both of the gallery's February exhibitions, this and Wildlife 2027), which covers printing at 16x12, 18x12 or 12x12 inches in gallery-owned frames. Selected participants have their work printed and hung in the gallery, shown in an online gallery on the website and included in an exhibition catalogue, receive a digital certificate of participation, have photos and video of the installed work shared on the gallery's social media, and are automatically put forward for its Photographer of the Month. Submit 1 to 8 JPEGs at 300ppi and at least 3,000 pixels on the shortest side, named Firstname-Surname, in one batch via Smash, WeTransfer or Dropbox to the gallery's submissions address, stating which exhibition you are entering, your nationality or country of residence and any links. Deadline 9 October 2026; acceptance notification by 14 October (only selected photographers are notified) and payment due by 28 October. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: Free (£50 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Myth, Folk & Superstition: Surreal Fables · Der Greif
item.description: Open call from Der Greif, the Munich non-profit for contemporary photography, for another edition of its Pulse online exhibitions, timed to launch on 31 October - "following on the heels of Halloween, just before Día de los Muertos and an upcoming Friday the 13th in November". The brief asks lens-based artists to explore modern folklore, cultural superstitions, myth-making and surrealism: from crossing paths with a black cat to honouring ancestors at vibrant altars, humans have always used stories, rituals and visual symbols to make sense of fate, luck and the unseen, and Der Greif wants photographic work that operates at the intersection of reality, fable and belief, whether staged cinematic storytelling, surreal dreamscapes or documentary studies of local legends, ancestral altars and talismanic objects. Selected artists are shown in an online exhibition in Der Greif's Pulse section, join an online roundtable critique with peers facilitated by Der Greif staff, and may be invited to submit a portfolio to Der Greif Studio, its route to artwork sales and commissions. Selection is on artistic quality, conceptual clarity, openness to dialogue and process, and engagement with themes of identity and community; the four staff jurors are named on the entry page. Submissions are one cohesive project not previously featured by Der Greif; the entry page and its upload form ask for at least 10 and up to 15 images, while the call's own conditions of participation say 1 to 10. Der Greif describes the submission as free with a suggested €10 donation, but the Picter entry page charges a flat €10; artists who cannot contribute can email the organiser for a 50% or 100% discount code. Open to photographers and videographers internationally, particularly emerging and mid-career artists, with no age or regional restriction. Deadline 14 October 2026 at 11:59pm CET; results are due on 30 October. — Deadline: October 14, 2026. Fee: €10 (waivers available). Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Torn Boundaries · Bristol Art Museum
item.description: National juried call for collage from Bristol Art Museum, the nonprofit museum on Wardwell Street in Bristol, Rhode Island, for a show in its main galleries from 31 January to 1 April 2027. Torn Boundaries asks artists to explore the boundaries that define, separate, connect and sometimes divide us - physical or psychological, personal or cultural, geographic or political, historical or imagined - and the prospectus frames collage as the means: cutting, tearing, layering, juxtaposition, fragmentation and recombination that disrupt established relationships, asking what happens when an edge is crossed, a border redrawn, a familiar image removed from its context. This is a collage call, not a photography call: the prospectus names no media beyond collage and carries no photography clause either way, so photomontage and photo-collage fit its own definition of the form while a straight photograph does not. The juror is Francine Weiss, an artist, art advisor and museum professional with curatorial posts at the National Gallery of Art, Harvard Art Museums, deCordova, Fitchburg Art Museum, the Photographic Resource Center and Newport Art Museum, and a PhD in American art and the history of photography from Boston University. Cash awards are promised but the amounts are not yet published. Entry is open to US residents aged 18 or over; up to three works may be entered ($25 for one, $35 for two, $45 for three) as JPEGs under 4 MB, works no larger than 40 inches in either direction (diptychs and triptychs count as one), unframed work accepted with clips, magnets or an alternative hanging system, with a statement of up to 200 words. Accepted work must arrive by 15 January 2027 - the prospectus says by UPS in one line and by US Postal Service in another - or be hand-delivered on 14 or 15 January with a prepaid return label; the museum takes no commission and puts collectors directly in touch with the artist. Reception 7 February 2027. Entries close at midnight on Sunday 29 November 2026 through OnlineJuriedShows. — Deadline: November 29, 2026. Fee: $25 (1 entry), $35 (2), $45 (3). Prize: Museum exhibition + Cash awards (amounts not yet published).

item.title: AUTOPORTRAIT 2026: PLAY · Kuala Lumpur Photo Awards
item.description: Third interim edition of Kuala Lumpur Photo Awards' AUTOPORTRAIT open call, run this year with FORMAT International Photography Festival and taking FORMAT's 2027 festival theme, PLAY, as its brief. KLPA frames self-portraiture as always grounded in experimentation, trial and error and creative playfulness, and reads PLAY widely - fun, joyful, exploratory, experimental, deceitful, mischievous, subversive or rule-bending - from camera play and questioning the medium itself to documenting the act of play. Prizes are €1,000, €500 and €300, and the top 35 finalists have their portraits promoted online and screened at FORMAT27 in Derby, United Kingdom (11 March to 11 April 2027) and at future KLPA exhibitions in Kuala Lumpur. The jury is Jodi Kwok (curator at QUAD and FORMAT), Enrico Stefanelli (founder and artistic director of Photolux Festival, Lucca), D. M. Terblanche (South African self-taught artist, 2026 New Eyes Award recipient), Mari Katayama (Japanese artist whose self-portraits use her own body as sculpture and lens) and Sean Cham (artist, historian and RCA tutor). Open to professional and amateur photographers from all countries aged 16 or over on the deadline date; each submission takes up to 10 single images with captions, priced €12 for one, €24 for two, €45 for three to six and €65 for seven to ten, with a maximum of two submissions per photographer, and full-time students under 25 may enter one image free with proof of enrolment, judged alongside the main category. All photographs must have been taken between 2024 and 2026 (proof may be requested at verification), and entries are judged blind. The rules bar commercial or advertising images, heavily manipulated, HDR or content-altered work, and AI prompt-generated images in whole or in part. The call opens on 25 September 2026 - entry will be through the KLPA site's ENTER link or its Picter page, with payment by card via Picter - and closes at midnight Malaysian time (UTC+8) on Wednesday 25 November 2026, unless extended. Jury selection in early December, shortlist in mid-January 2027 and prizewinners announced in February 2027. — Deadline: November 25, 2026. Fee: €12 (1 image), €24 (2), €45 (3–6), €65 (7–10); students under 25 free for 1 image. Prize: €1,000 + €500 + €300 + Screening at FORMAT27 Derby (top 35).

item.title: International Photography Exhibition 168 (IPE 168) · Royal Photographic Society
item.description: The Royal Photographic Society's International Photography Exhibition has been held almost every year since 1854 and calls itself the world's longest-running contemporary photography exhibition; the 168th edition opened for entries on 15 September 2026 and closes at 23:59 GMT on Tuesday 15 December 2026, with an extra day to 16 December to finalise entries already started. Anyone of any age or level of practice, anywhere in the world, can enter, and RPS membership is not required. There is no theme and no categories: the T&Cs say there is no restriction on genre, process or technique, that film and digital, experimental and traditional processes are all eligible, that manipulation in software or the darkroom is allowed, and that found photographs may be incorporated - but work that includes generative AI in whole or in part is not eligible. Every entrant gets one free single-image entry; further entries, each of four images from one series or four single images, cost £35 (£27 for RPS members, £20 for under-30s), and multiple paid entries are allowed, with an early-bird prize draw for entries in by 19 October. The RPS longlists, a changing guest selection panel shortlists, and shortlisted photographers are then asked to send prints for a final anonymous selection of about 100 works, which the RPS mounts and frames at its own cost for a touring exhibition at partner venues; the RPS would not normally exhibit work larger than 50 x 60 cm. Awards are the £1,000 IPE Award and the £1,000 Under 30s Award (each with a year's RPS membership), a two-week solo exhibition at an RPS partner venue, four RPS Journal features chosen by the editor, five Selectors' Spotlight statements, and digital and social-media exposure for shortlisted work. Copyright stays with the photographer; the RPS takes a four-year promotional licence. The selection panel had not been named on the RPS site at the time of listing, and no notification date is published. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: Free (one single image); £35 per further entry (£27 RPS members, £20 under 30). Prize: £1,000 IPE Award + £1,000 Under 30s Award + 100-print touring exhibition + Solo exhibition + RPS Journal publication features.

item.title: Lucky Star Issue 6: Womanhood & Femininity
item.description: Lucky Star is an independent photography magazine made in San Francisco by Madison Blanchard and sold through Green Apple Books and Beeks Books in the Bay Area and Waste Store in London. Its sixth issue is themed on womanhood and femininity: the call asks for projects about what it means to be a woman in society, women's empowerment, girlhood, female relationships, what femininity means and represents, how body and object contribute to those ideas, and social norms and the breaking of them, with the interpretation left entirely to the artist. Any medium of photo-based artwork is welcome, but it must be submitted as a series or body of work of at least five images, and ongoing projects are accepted. Only women, femme and female-identifying artists may submit to this issue; artists from anywhere and of any age are welcome. The deadline is Tuesday 13 October 2026 at 11:59pm Pacific. Entry is through a Google Form linked from the magazine's Submit page; the form requires a Google sign-in to open, so the fee, if any, could not be read - neither the magazine's site nor its own announcement mentions one, and the previous issue was free to enter. — Deadline: October 13, 2026. Fee: See website. Prize: Publication.

item.title: River Margin — Spotlight: Ecologies
item.description: River Margin is a new ecology journal whose website runs a print issue alongside online segments; Spotlight: Ecologies is an annual online strand that highlights work on three named ecological topics, and for 2026 the three are Urban (Wild) Ecologies (wildness within the built environment - plants in cracks, neglected structures, material ecologies, repair and reuse, multispecies habitation), Nocturnal Ecologies (the worlds that become perceptible after dark - moths, bats, night-blooming plants, artificial light, bioluminescence, darkness and perception) and Arctic Ecologies (the flora, fauna, fungi and landscapes of Arctic and subarctic regions, from sea ice and permafrost to lichens and traditional ecological knowledge). Each topic takes photography and visual art (up to seven images by Google Drive link or email attachment, not WeTransfer) and writing (any form up to 10,000 words as one PDF). Submissions go to the journal's email address with the subject line for the chosen topic - 'SPOTLIGHT: Urban Ecologies Submission', 'SPOTLIGHT: Nocturnal Ecologies Submission' or 'SPOTLIGHT: Arctic Ecologies Submission' - by 1 October 2026, after which the strand launches online. There is no entry fee, artists retain full rights, no AI is accepted in any category, and only successful submissions receive a reply. This is the online segment; the journal's print Issue 1 (closing 1 November) is listed separately. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online publication.

item.title: Exhibition Proposals — Q4 2026 · Holter Museum of Art
item.description: The Holter Museum of Art in Helena, Montana mounts twenty to twenty-five solo and group exhibitions a year across three main galleries and two smaller ones, each running six weeks to three months, and fills part of that programme from artist proposals reviewed on a rolling quarterly basis. Four selection dates are set each year; the final 2026 round has a submission deadline of December 6 for a December 9 review, and it is the last chance before the 2027 cycle. Applicants hear back within two weeks of the selection date, but the museum organises exhibitions one to three years in advance, so a successful proposal is not a near-term show. Proposals are accepted from artists nationwide and internationally, and two or more artists may propose together. A proposal takes a cover letter giving the exhibition title, a description of the concept, content and medium, and the method of delivery; an artist statement, biography and CV; any educational programming or community outreach on offer; a budget and any special accommodations; an image list with titles, dimensions, years and media; and ten high-quality images, with up to twenty accepted, uploaded as individual files (PDF for everything else, no HEIC). The online form charges a $20 application fee on its second step. The museum shows photography as a matter of course - its Baucus Gallery solo this autumn, Jessica Hays's The Sun Sets Midafternoon, is by a Montana photographer working in pigment prints, artist books and historic photographic processes. — Deadline: December 6, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Here & Now · Bristol Art Museum
item.description: Bristol Art Museum, a nonprofit museum on Wardwell Street in Bristol, Rhode Island, closes its year-long recognition of America's 250th anniversary by turning from national history to the place it calls home. Here & Now is a regional juried exhibition of work inspired by Rhode Island, the greater Narragansett Bay area or the Southern New England region: the prospectus lists photography first among the media it brings together, alongside painting, printmaking, fiber, mixed media and other two- and three-dimensional work, and the subjects it suggests run from coastal landscapes, Bristol Harbor and working waterfronts to architecture, neighbourhoods, natural environments, community life and personal interpretations of place, whether representational or conceptual. The juror is Dan Wallace, a RISD-trained landscape architect with Sudbury Design Group since 1985. Selected works hang in the Livingston Gallery from December 6, 2026 to January 10, 2027, with a reception on December 6 from 2 to 4pm; the museum's other galleries show harbour photographs by featured Bristol artist Brendon Adams and new work from its 2026 Harbor Residency at the same time. Entry is open to artists in Rhode Island and the surrounding region who can hand-deliver accepted work on November 23 or 24 (no shipped work is accepted); work must have been completed in 2026, be no more than 40 inches in any direction (3D work under 50 lb), and up to three pieces may be entered - $15 for one, $25 for two, $35 for three - as JPEGs under 4 MB. The show is part of the museum's annual fundraising, and exhibiting artists agree to donate 50% of any sale to the museum. Entries close Sunday November 8, 2026 through OnlineJuriedShows. — Deadline: November 8, 2026. Fee: $15 (1 entry), $25 (2), $35 (3). Prize: Museum exhibition.

item.title: Where Stories Gather · WaterWorks Art Museum
item.description: The WaterWorks Art Museum sits on the banks of the Yellowstone River in Miles City, Montana, in a 1910 water plant listed on the National Register of Historic Places - its galleries are the renovated basins that produced the town's drinking water for sixty years - and it has run an annual juried show since at least 2014 (the 2018 edition was titled Photography Plus). The 2026-27 edition, Where Stories Gather, invites artists working in two- and three-dimensional media to explore the places, memories, objects, traditions and encounters where narratives take shape, from landscapes, homes and communities to personal histories, cultural symbols and quiet moments of reflection. The prospectus names no media list beyond 2D and 3D, so photographers should note that eligibility is unenumerated; the museum's own juried-show history includes a photography edition. The juror is Jenn Hall Tooke, a museum artist and paleontology-trained community advocate who has worked at WaterWorks and the Carter County Museum in Ekalaka. Six cash awards: $300 Best in Show, $200, $150 and $100 honourable mentions, a $150 Director's Choice and a $100 People's Choice. Entries are open to artists nationwide; work must be original, made within the last two years, at least 12 inches on one side and no more than 60 inches in any direction, and for sale (35% commission). A $40 fee covers up to three entries, judged from digital images, with results emailed by December 22; accepted work is due January 14, the show runs from the January 29, 2027 reception to March 18, and a committee picks about 25 pieces for a smaller collection that tours galleries in eastern Montana for the rest of 2027. Shipping both ways is at the artist's expense, and an artist who withdraws an accepted piece is barred from the museum's juried shows for three years. Deadline Wednesday December 16, 2026 through OnlineJuriedShows. — Deadline: December 16, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 3 entries). Prize: $300 Best in Show + $200 / $150 / $100 honourable mentions + $150 Director's Choice + $100 People's Choice + Museum exhibition + Traveling exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Reflection Art Show · Paul Nigra Center for Creative Arts
item.description: The Paul Nigra Center for Creative Arts is a community arts centre in Gloversville, New York, run by The Arc Lexington, that mounts several open art shows a year (its Winter, Regional and New York State Summer shows draw 40 to 60 artists each, and it hosts an annual show of Adirondack Life magazine's photography contest winners). The 2026 Reflection Art Show invites artists everywhere to submit works of any medium and any subject - 'your best new art, or reflect on the past by showing off your favorite pieces from your portfolio' - to close out 2026 and welcome 2027. Up to three works cost $25 ($15 for centre members), with up to two more at $10 each ($7 for members). Work must be original and not previously shown at the centre, hanging pieces may not exceed 25 pounds, and content with nudity or sexual themes is not accepted because of the centre's family audience. Entries can be made through OnlineJuriedShows, through the centre's own Google Form, or by mailing or emailing the prospectus form. Selection notifications go out by October 7; accepted work must be delivered or shipped to arrive by October 24 (shipped work carries a $10 handling fee and needs a prepaid return label), and the show runs October 30, 2026 to January 7, 2027 with a public reception on November 5 from 4 to 7pm. Awards and prizes are funded by supporters and announced November 4, but the amounts are not published. The centre takes 20% on sales; work need not be for sale. Deadline October 4, 2026. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: $25 for up to 3 works ($15 members); $10 per additional work up to 5. Prize: Exhibition + Awards at reception.

item.title: Open Space: Art About the Land 2026 · Minnetrista Museum & Gardens
item.description: Since 2001 Open Space: Art About the Land has asked Indiana artists to draw creative inspiration from the land and celebrate the idea of open space. It is an annual juried competition and exhibition developed by Minnetrista Museum & Gardens in Muncie and the Anderson Museum of Art in partnership with Red-tail Land Conservancy, and the 2026 show hangs at both museums from November 7, 2026 to January 3, 2027, with a portion of proceeds going to the conservancy's habitat work. Any artist 18 or older who is a present or former resident of Indiana may enter up to three works made in the last three years for one $35 fee; eligible work is listed as ceramics, digital art, drawings, fiber, mixed media, paintings, prints, sculptures, metalwork and photography (digital work must be printed; video and audio are not eligible), it must address 'the spirit of open space with reference to the land', may not have been made as part of a class, and may not exceed 50 pounds; the two surfaces disagree on size - the org's prospectus PDF caps entries at 60 inches in any direction while the ShowSubmit entry page says 48 inches. The ShowSubmit entry page also states that no use of artificial intelligence, in the conception or development of the artwork, is permitted (the PDF carries no AI clause). The juror is India Cruse-Griffin, a Muncie-trained mixed-media collage artist and Harrison Center studio artist who won the Indy Arts Council's DeHaan Artist of Distinction in 2025. Awards total $1,500 at her discretion: $500, $350 and $250 for first to third place, $100 merit awards for photography, three-dimensional work and the Jim Faulkner landscape award, and the $100 Stefan and Joan Anderson Prize for the best piece representing a Red-tail nature preserve. Results are emailed October 2; accepted work is dropped off by appointment on October 16 or 17, the awards reception is November 6 at Minnetrista, and both venues take 30% on sales. Entries close at 11:59pm on Monday September 28, 2026 through ShowSubmit. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 3 works). Prize: $1,500 in cash awards ($100 photography merit award) + Museum exhibition at two venues.

item.title: In Between Gallery Open Call 2026 · Fabrica
item.description: Fabrica is a contemporary art gallery in a Grade II-listed former church in Brighton's Lanes, founded as an artist-led space in 1996. Its In Between Gallery turns the gallery's picture window on Duke Street - one of the city's busiest pedestrianised streets, busy into the night - into a temporary photography gallery, and this ninth-year open call, run with Spectrum Photographic, Photo Fringe, Jane & Jeremy and POST, seeks one image by one UK-based photographer or artist group who considers themselves early to mid-career. The selected image is exhibited from November 2026 to April 2027 (with occasional short removals around venue hire), and the artist receives a £350 fee covering the exhibition, a talk at Fabrica's Photography Networking Event on Thursday 4 February 2027 (travel paid separately) and an Instagram takeover from 28 January to 4 February; the artist and image are also promoted by Fabrica and its partners. Practicalities that the panel weighs: the window is roughly 2.7 by 2.25 metres, so square formats sit well, and its light filter does not favour predominantly dark or black-and-white images. There is no theme and no entry fee, and the call is open to UK residents only. Applications go through a Google Form with up to three low-res images, a title and context document, a biography or CV, and a link to a website or Instagram; the deadline is 12 noon on Monday 26 October 2026 and the selected artist is told on Friday 30 October. — Deadline: October 26, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £350 fee + Window gallery exhibition (Nov 2026 – Apr 2027) + Artist talk.

item.title: Unfold — Fabrica x Sussex Contemporary Open Call 2027
item.description: Sussex Contemporary, an independent arts organisation that stages curated exhibitions and artist opportunities across South East England, and Fabrica, the contemporary art gallery in a Grade II-listed former church in Brighton's Lanes, follow their first partnership exhibition Resonance (2026) with Unfold, a UK-wide judged open call whose selected works are shown at Fabrica from 16 April to 9 May 2027. The theme - to reveal, develop or become; an idea taking shape, a landscape changing, a practice growing over time - is offered as a starting point rather than a constraint, and the organisers say they are as interested in process as in outcome and in the stories behind the work. Original work in any discipline is welcome, with photography named alongside drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, jewellery, illustration, mixed media, installation, moving image, sound and performance (giclée and other reproduction prints are refused as printmaking entries). Entry is open to amateur and professional artists with a UK connection - born, educated, living or working in the UK, or another clear link. Each work costs £20 to enter, up to three per artist, bought through the Sussex Contemporary shop, after which a closed artist page links the submission form; selection is by an independent five-person panel, announced through the call, of which the first named is Fabrica co-director Liz Whitehead, and is anonymous wherever possible. Two prizes follow selection without a separate application: the WeAreBrighton Prize (a year of the monthly WeAreBrighton talks plus mentoring with Sussex Contemporary founder Jo Myles) and Unfold in the Window, a further showing in Fabrica's Duke Street window gallery between May and September 2027. All selected work is for sale with a commission to Sussex Contemporary; there is no hanging fee, but delivery and collection are the artist's cost. The call opened in August 2026 and closes at 11:59pm on 21 February 2027, with artists notified in the week of 8 March and drop-off on 12 April. — Deadline: February 21, 2027. Fee: £20 per work (up to 3). Prize: Exhibition at Fabrica + Mentoring prize + Window gallery showing (May–Sep 2027).

item.title: ZONE 6 — Collective Photobook Open Call · Zone Magazine
item.description: ZONE is an independent book publisher and photography-based visual arts platform started in 2018 and run by its founder Ali Beşikçi as a one-person operation; this is the open call for its sixth collective book, after five earlier volumes that between them published more than 650 artists from around the world. There is deliberately no theme. The interest is in what happens when images from different contexts are placed together and begin to act like parts of a larger organism, so the call is open worldwide to all visual arts - photography first, but also painting, illustration, sculpture, design, film stills, anything printable in a book - with no restriction on age, accomplishments or approach. You may send images from one or more projects; they are considered individually, and selection is said to rest solely on the images, not on CV or status, with a stated preference for giving visibility to lesser-known artists. Selected artists are published in the sixth collective book in offset print, with print run, size and design decided by the character of the work; the curator selects, edits and sequences the images and places them alongside other works, but will not crop or alter them without consent. Favourite works are also shared on ZONE's social channels during and after the call, whether or not they make the book. Selected artists do not receive a free copy but may buy any number at 50% off. There are two ways to enter: pay a €10 submission fee for up to 10 images, or pre-order the book at the early-bird price of €30, which includes one submission of up to 10 images; both are non-refundable and neither guarantees inclusion, and every additional submission needs its own fee or pre-order. Payment through the page redirects to an upload form; files are JPEGs under 2 MB named First Last Number.jpg, with your Instagram username in the message, and submissions that ignore the naming rules may be excluded without refund. High-resolution files are requested only if selected. Deadline 30 November 2026; featured artists are announced on 1 February 2027 on the website, social media and newsletter, and the book is due in spring 2027. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: €10 (up to 10 images) or €30 book pre-order incl. submission. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: Germaine Van Parys Award 2026
item.description: Named for Belgium's first female photojournalist, who made her debut at Le Soir in 1918 and founded the Van Parys agency in 1956, the Germaine Van Parys Award is a Brussels-based programme for women photographers working in a documentary approach, organised by the non-profit Out of Focus and now in its third edition after laureates in 2024 and 2025. The 2026 call runs from 15 September to 1 December 2026 and is open to women photographers of all ages and nationalities, including anyone who identifies as a woman; applications are free and may be written in French, Dutch or English. There are two categories. The Germaine Van Parys Award itself is a €8,000 production grant for a professional photographer - one whose work has previously been exhibited or published - to make an unpublished documentary project related to Brussels over ten months; the money is meant for production, travel, equipment, developing and digitising, while the organiser covers exhibition prints and framing for the show that follows. The Germaine Van Parys Mentorship selects five women photographers residing in Belgium for ten monthly in-person sessions in Brussels, held in French on the first Thursday of the month from February 2027, with a €1,000 grant each towards a project of their own choosing; applicants must be able to take part in French and commit to all ten dates. Both strands end with a Brussels exhibition in January 2028 - the award winner's finished work shown alongside a projection of the mentorship projects - and the award project is also published as a portfolio in Médor magazine. Applications go through a form on the website as a single PDF of no more than 10 MB: for the award, a CV of up to two pages, a short biography, 10 to 15 images and a project statement on the Brussels subject; for the mentorship, a CV, biography, 15 images, a project description and a motivation letter. One project per applicant. A jury of photography and visual-arts professionals will be published on the website; winners are announced on 21 December 2026 and must be available for a meeting on 7 January 2027. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €8,000 production grant + 5 × €1,000 mentorship grants + Exhibition.

item.title: River Margin — Water Bodies
item.description: Water Bodies is an online segment of River Margin, the ecology-and-botany journal founded in 2026 by Melbourne-based artist, musician and writer Lana Eileen, whose first issue is still assembling separately. This call is narrower and faster: work about bodies of water - rivers, streams, lakes, the ocean, wetlands and more - and about water's relationship to plants, animals and people, water histories and water stories, to be featured online. Photographers may send up to seven photographs, digital or film, as email attachments or through a Google Drive link (the journal asks entrants not to use WeTransfer, as the links expire before it can open them). The same call takes writing up to 10,000 words, sound art and music, film, and visual art; for visual art the journal accepts only painting, drawing, sculpture and traditional media, ruling out digital and AI-generated work - the no-AI rule is written under visual art, while photography is described simply as digital or film. Work must be in English but is welcome from anywhere in the world, and you may submit to more than one category as long as each follows its own rules; a short third-person bio and a link to your website or social media are helpful but not required. There is no fee and no payment: the journal says plainly that it is a volunteer-run project by one artist and cannot yet pay contributors, so the return is publication online. Submissions go by email with the subject Water Bodies Submission by 27 September 2026; because of the volume received, only successful entrants hear back, within two months of submitting, and the journal asks that nobody email to confirm receipt. — Deadline: September 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online publication.

item.title: Paralaje Magazine — No. 2: Fine Art Black & White
item.description: Paralaje is an independent contemporary photography magazine published in Spanish with English translation, in print and digital editions, directed and edited by George Riverón; its name borrows the astronomy term parallax for the idea that no image is absolute and everything changes with the point from which you look. After a first issue built from an open call, the second call is dedicated to black-and-white fine art photography: series in which light, shadow, form, the body, space, memory, intimacy or abstraction come together into a visual language of their own. The editors say they are not after a particular aesthetic or a closed definition of fine art, but want personal, coherent projects that can sustain a point of view across a series, and they will judge on the visual strength of the images, the coherence of the series and the distinctiveness of the approach. Any photographic process qualifies - digital, film, alternative processes or experimental techniques - and the call is open to photographers of any country, background, age or level of experience. A submission is a series of 4 to 8 black-and-white photographs with a title, a short statement, a short biography, city and country of residence, and a website or Instagram if you have one, sent through a Google Form linked from the call page. Selected series appear in Paralaje No. 2, dated October 2026, in both the print and digital editions, with the magazine reserving a final editorial pick of which images from each chosen series are printed. There is no submission fee, no payment or free copy is mentioned, and the deadline is 30 September 2026. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication in print & digital.

item.title: Home Fires: 37th Annual Members' Show · Tulsa Artists' Coalition
item.description: The Tulsa Artists' Coalition is a volunteer-run non-profit gallery in the Tulsa Arts District that mounts around eleven exhibitions a year at no cost to the exhibiting artists; Home Fires is its 37th annual members' show, pitched as a celebration of Tulsa's art community and the bonds that make TAC a place to come home to. It is open to all media with no restriction on subject beyond hate speech, and it is a members' show in the buyable sense: new and renewing memberships are accepted up to and including the submission deadline, and membership runs from $35 for an individual ($15 for full-time students, $50 per household), so a photographer anywhere can enter by joining, though accepted work must be delivered to the gallery on 26-27 December 2026 and unsold work collected on 23-24 January 2027. Members may submit up to two original pieces made in the last two years, one form per piece, as JPEGs of at least 1,200 pixels on the long side; because of the gallery's size only one piece per artist is selected, and work may be no larger than 24 inches on its longest side and must arrive ready to hang. Selection is from the digital submissions by a Selections Committee of three jurors - artists, educators and other art professionals, changed every year - with accepted and declined artists emailed by 5 December 2026. The show runs 1-23 January 2027 with the opening at the First Friday Art Crawl on 1 January, where a Grand Prize and three juror's choice cash awards are announced; the amounts are not published. Submissions opened 8 September and close at midnight Central time on 7 November 2026 through the coalition's Submittable portal, where the entry form carries no fee. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: Free (TAC membership required; from $35, students $15). Prize: Cash awards (Grand Prize + 3 juror's choice) + Exhibition.

item.title: Kerkini Wetlands Photo Award 2026
item.description: A new annual international photography award dedicated to Lake Kerkini in Northern Greece, a Ramsar-listed wetland with more than 300 bird species and, in the organiser's words, one of Europe's premier destinations for wildlife and bird photography. The 2026 edition is the first, organised by Agkistro Action, a social cooperative in the Serres region, and it is built as a conservation platform rather than a tourism promotion: the stated aim is to build a lasting visual archive of the lake and to promote environmental awareness through photography. Four categories - Birds of Kerkini, Wildlife of the Wetland, Wetland Landscape, and Human & Wetland - and the one hard rule is geographic: every photograph must have been taken within Lake Kerkini National Park or its surrounding wetland ecosystem, though there is no restriction on when it was taken, so archive work from earlier visits qualifies. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide aged 18 and over; entrants aged 18 to 25 are automatically considered for the Young Photographer of the Year Award. The entry fee is €15 per participant for up to 10 photographs across one or more categories, submitted as JPEGs through Picter. The prize fund is €3,000: €1,000 for Photo of the Year, €400 for each of the four category winners, and €400 for the Young Photographer award, plus trophies, up to five special mentions, and a place in the official exhibition for winning and shortlisted work. The jury is Costas Vidakis, Ellie Rothnie, Emil Enchev and Nikos Petrou, judging anonymously. The rules run to a detailed ethical-wildlife code (no baiting, no captive animals, no sky replacement or compositing) and ban images generated or altered with AI, while AI-based noise reduction and sharpening are allowed. Photographers keep copyright and grant only a non-exclusive, non-commercial, credited licence tied to the award. Submissions run 20 September to 20 November 2026; finalists are announced on 5 January 2027 and winners at the awards ceremony on World Wetlands Day, 2 February 2027. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: €15. Prize: €3,000 in prizes + Exhibition.

item.title: Call for Artists: 2027 Exhibition Season · Red Brick Center for the Arts
item.description: The Red Brick Center for the Arts, the City of Aspen's arts centre, invites artists living and working in Colorado to apply for its 2027 exhibition season. The programme runs solo exhibitions in the West Gallery and curated group exhibitions in the Main Gallery, and artists selected through this call are considered for the four 2027 slots: 11 February to 26 March, 10 June to 31 July, 12 August to 15 October, and 2 December 2027 to 10 January 2028. There is no fee to apply. The Gallery Committee reviews submissions and recommends artists whose work, in the centre's words, demonstrates artistic excellence, originality, and meaningful engagement with contemporary ideas and practices; the Red Brick's recent programme includes the 2025 Colorado Juried Exhibition and a solo show by the photographer Wendi Schneider. Photography is named outright in the accepted media, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, ceramics, textiles, sculpture, mixed media and experimental work, and proposed work must not have been exhibited at the Red Brick before. Applicants submit an artist statement and biography, 8 to 12 images of recent work labelled with title, dimensions and medium, and a 250 to 500 word exhibition proposal describing the themes, any new work planned for 2027, and how it relates to the wider practice; a CV and website are optional. Artists are responsible for delivery and return shipping; work is offered for sale during the show with a 60/40 split in the artist's favour, and the exhibition agreement asks that photographs and other paper works be framed under glass or Plexiglas unless another presentation is agreed. Applications close 30 September 2026 and artists are notified on 6 November 2026. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: TAC Gallery 2027 Exhibition Submissions · Tulsa Artists' Coalition
item.description: The Tulsa Artists' Coalition, a 501(c)(3) that runs TAC Gallery in the Tulsa Arts District, is taking proposals for its 2027 exhibition season. The gallery at 9 East Reconciliation Way mounts a new exhibition every calendar month, and artists may propose a solo show, a collaboration with other artists, or a themed group show they would curate. Submissions in all media and disciplines are eligible, subject to the physical constraints of the space - two 24-foot main walls that take work up to 11 feet high - with an emphasis on the contemporary perspective and a body of work with a consistent style or theme. Work should have been completed within the last several years (unless a retrospective) and not shown in Tulsa in the last two years. Read the geography before applying: the Coalition's mission is to support artists in Tulsa and the surrounding area, so out-of-area proposals are accepted but capped at two per eleven-month season, and artists living in Tulsa temporarily, on a fellowship for instance, count as out of area. There is no submission fee. Applicants upload ten images or video with brief descriptions including media and dimensions, a statement of the proposed exhibit's theme, and a bio or resume, through Submittable. A Selections Committee of three jurors - artists, educators and other art professionals, changed each year - reviews the proposals and the 2027 schedule is settled by 15 November 2026. TAC provides installation help, a First Friday opening reception, press and social promotion, and volunteer gallery sitting, and has historically absorbed most exhibition costs; artists cover shipping both ways, provide statements and a price list, and TAC retains a 35% commission on sales (30% for members). The gallery carries no insurance on exhibited work. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Shifting Grounds: 38th Annual Prince George's County Juried Exhibition · Brentwood Arts Exchange
item.description: The 38th annual Prince George's County Juried Exhibition, run by the Arts and Cultural Heritage Division of M-NCPPC's Department of Parks and Recreation and shown at the Brentwood Arts Exchange, the anchor institution of Maryland's Gateway Arts District, from 16 November 2026 to 9 January 2027. This year's theme, Shifting Grounds, asks artists to reflect on transformation across personal life, community, technology and environment - how we adapt, resist or redefine ourselves as identities and ideologies reconfigure - and the organisers say it should be interpreted broadly. The juror is Chris Combs, a Washington DC and Mount Rainier artist whose sculptural work incorporates and questions technology; he was 2025 Artist in Residence at the Sanford Underground Research Facility, a five-time DC Commission on the Arts and Humanities fellow, and a former photo editor for National Geographic. Photography is named in the eligible media, alongside painting, drawing, assemblage, fiber, video, printmaking, encaustic, glass, metal, collage and mixed media; work made with generative AI will not be selected, and reproductions are out. Open to artists 18 and over who live, work, study or keep a studio in Prince George's County, Maryland, with up to three artworks each, no size limit, and no work previously shown in this exhibition. There is no entry fee, but every participant must complete M-NCPPC's one-time online vendor registration (a W-9 is needed) so that the county can pay them: each artist selected receives a $150 participation stipend after the show closes, and on the juror's recommendation the Division may purchase works for the M-NCPPC Permanent Art Collection. M-NCPPC insures consigned work for 75% of its sale value and takes a 25% commission on sales. Submissions close at 11:59pm on 23 October 2026; selected artists are notified by 28 October, work is dropped off on 7 or 9 November, and the reception is Saturday 21 November, 3 to 5pm. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $150 stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: Idea Capital Awards 2027
item.description: Idea Capital is an Atlanta grassroots funder, launched in 2008, that pools small donations from the city's arts community and hands the money straight to artists for new, experimental projects - in its own words, audacious art that traditional funding sources would find difficult to champion. Two award levels, decided by the panel rather than requested by the applicant: the Catalyst Award, a $1,000 stipend for emerging artists or a small or early-stage project, and the Vanguard Award, $2,500 for more established artists or projects further along in development. A third, the $5,000 Susan Antinori Visual Artist Award, is limited to painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics or mixed media, so photographers should read themselves into the two general awards; the Margaret Kargbo Artist As Activist designation goes at the committee's discretion to a project embodying social justice. Eligible disciplines run across visual art, digital media, film, video, performance, curatorial projects and more, and the test is whether form, process or content take a real risk - work executed in traditional ways throughout is not a fit, and neither are completed projects, thesis work, or art that is secondary to education, therapy or activism. Funds cover materials, equipment, fabrication, artist and professional fees, plus research and development such as travel or residencies, but not standard framing or mounting shows outside Atlanta. Open to working artists and cultural producers aged 20 and over living in metro Atlanta, including collectives, curators and educators; students may apply for work outside their academic programme; past awardees wait three years. One application per artist, submitted free through Submittable with a general project budget rather than line items. Applications close at 11:59pm on 1 November 2026; a shortlist is announced 1 December, awards on 7 January 2027, and funds are disbursed on 21 January. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000 / $2,500 stipends.

item.title: 2027 Grants for Artists · Arts Foundation of Cape Cod
item.description: The Arts Foundation of Cape Cod's annual Grants for Artists put $500 to $10,000 into the hands of individual artists, culture bearers and creative practitioners living in Barnstable, Dukes and Nantucket counties - Cape Cod, Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket - for projects carried out during the 2027 calendar year. The foundation raises the money from its own donors and sponsors, and the 2027 round prioritises work that creates access to the arts for everyone: projects that remove financial, physical or social barriers, engage seniors, people with disabilities or intergenerational groups, and foster connection across the Cape and Islands. All disciplines are welcome - performing, visual, literary and media - and the eligibility bar is a practising artist aged 18 or over, recognised by peers or critics as committed to producing work regularly, with at least a two-year history of public engagement, presentation or publication, who is the lead artist on the project and produces work that benefits and focuses primarily on the region. Students pursuing any degree are not eligible, funding must be used between 1 January and 31 December 2027, and repeat funding for the same activity is not expected beyond a year. There is no application fee. Applications opened 8 September and close at 11:59pm on Friday 6 November 2026, with awards announced in December 2026 and a final report due within 30 days of finishing the funded work. The foundation runs two one-hour virtual information sessions, on 1 October and 23 October at 10am, and publishes the grant rubric its committee scores against. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $500–$10,000.

item.title: 2027 Fellowships and Grants · Asian Cultural Council
item.description: The Asian Cultural Council has funded cultural exchange between the United States and Asia since 1963 - more than $100 million across nearly 6,000 exchanges - and its 2027 grant cycle opens on 1 October 2026. For photographers, who apply under Visual Art, the relevant programmes are the Individual Fellowship and, for artists based in Asia, the New York Fellowship. The Individual Fellowship funds one to six months of self-directed research, exploration and cultural immersion in a country new or less familiar to the applicant - meeting peers, visiting institutions, joining workshops, working in archives - with a maximum award of $35,000; it can be a joint fellowship of up to three artists sharing the same goals. The New York Fellowship brings a cohort from Asia to live in New York for six months, free from any obligation to produce or present work, with ACC support, group programming and optional housing at International House. Both are explicitly not production grants: ACC will not fund a documentary shoot, research for a planned book or exhibition, a residency to make new work, or travel to a single event. Applicants must be citizens or permanent residents of the US or one of 25 listed Asian countries and regions, at least 21, with five years of professional experience, and may not propose travel to the country they currently live in; funded activity must fall between 1 August 2027 and 31 December 2028. Applications go through ACC's GoApply portal from 1 October and close at 9:59am US Eastern on 10 November 2026, with letters of recommendation due by 16 November; decisions follow a November-to-April review and are sent in mid-May 2027. There is no application fee, and applicants may apply to only one programme per cycle. — Deadline: November 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Fellowship up to $35,000.

item.title: Artists in Queens Grant 2027 · Flushing Town Hall
item.description: Flushing Town Hall's Artists in Queens Grant gives $5,000 to individual artists who live in Queens for the creation of new work in a community setting. It is part of the New York State Council on the Arts' Statewide Community Regrants programme, which Flushing Town Hall administers for the borough, and per NYSCA's guidelines the peer panel will select ten artists for the 2027 round. Applicants make a single $5,000 request for a project that strengthens community bonds, widens access to cultural activities in Queens, advances the artist's career and engages the community: every funded project must include a community engagement component, such as a public exhibition or performance, and applications that build the community into the creative process - interviews, workshops, parallel work by a community group, an artist talk - are described as more competitive. Visual arts, digital and electronic arts, film and video and interdisciplinary work are all listed disciplines. Flushing Town Hall says it will not support projects created through AI platforms or generated through AI processes: every submission must be the result of the artist's own manual effort. Applicants must be current Queens residents with dated proof of residency, at least 18, and not enrolled in a full-time degree programme during the grant period; unincorporated collectives may apply through a Queens-based lead artist. Artists who applied directly to NYSCA in FY27, last year's grantees, and Flushing Town Hall staff and board are excluded. First-time applicants must attend or watch an information session before applying; sessions run from 28 September (virtual) through October, with Spanish and Mandarin-interpreted sessions, followed by Friday office hours and one-on-one application review days as the deadline nears. There is no fee. Applications opened 14 September and close at 5pm on Tuesday 1 December 2026, with notification in March 2027. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000.

item.title: Tendon Magazine Issue 09: Witness
item.description: Tendon is a literary and visual arts journal printed and published by the Johns Hopkins Center for Medical Humanities and Social Medicine in Baltimore, now eight issues in (Borders, Reflections on Trauma, Writing from Disaster, Breath, Sanctuary, Injury, Rest, Care). Issue 09 takes the theme of witness - to be present and observant at a particular place and time, to testify, to see with one's own eyes - and the editors list the positions a witness can occupy: bystander, advocate, adversary, ally, sentinel, caregiver, friend, archivist, documentarian, poet. They ask who is believed, whose testimony carries authority, how power and agency are tangled in the act of bearing witness, and when documenting becomes an obligation or a burden, with particular attention to medicine and care - witnessing illness, death, pain and systemic failures in healthcare, and what palliative care asks of those who accompany the dying. A second strand is witness across long arcs of time: what bodies, landscapes, ecosystems and infrastructures retain of human violence and environmental change, and how art can preserve what institutions have ignored; the call also names the unstable territory between witness and voyeur, proximity and intrusion, which is documentary photography's own question. Visual art submissions may be photography, painting, illustration, sculpture, ceramics, mixed media, digital art, comics, film or video and installation; you may submit one to three pieces with a short description, as TIFF, PNG, JPEG or PDF at 300 dpi, with priority to work that translates well to print. Submissions are free through Submittable and close on 1 November 2026, or earlier if a genre reaches its cap. Tendon takes First North American Serial Rights, including reprint in its own anthologies and promotion; all other rights stay with the contributor and revert on publication. No payment is mentioned. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: 46th Annual Faber Birren National Color Show · Stamford Art Association
item.description: The Stamford Art Association's 46th Faber Birren National Color Award Exhibit, which the Association calls the only artistic event devoted exclusively to the use of colour. Faber Birren, the colour consultant and author of 27 books on colour, endowed the award in 1980 with prizes for original and creative expression of colour, and his family still funds the cash awards; what began as a regional exhibit is now international in scope. Forty artists are selected by the juror and shown at the Association's three-storey Townhouse Gallery in Stamford and online. The juror this year is Jordan Hillman, Assistant Curator of Art at the Bruce Museum, previously a curatorial research assistant in the Department of Prints, Drawings and Photographs at the Baltimore Museum of Art, whose exhibition Odilon Redon and the Specter of Science opens at the Bruce in February 2027. The accepted media list is painting, mixed media, sculpture, photography, drawing and printmaking, so photography is named outright; the eligibility prose asks for original art in any two-dimensional or three-dimensional media created in the last three years and not previously shown in the Faber Birren exhibit, and only electronic media, performance art and installations are excluded. Awards come to over $1,600, with $1,000 for first place plus second, third and honourable mentions at the juror's discretion; winners are asked to take part in a video presentation. Entry is $35 for a non-member's first piece and $30 for a member's, plus $15 for each additional entry up to nine works per artist, and multiple entries must be submitted together to get the lower additional rate. Work may be up to 48 by 60 inches framed and sculpture up to 60 pounds. Submissions close at 11:59pm on 9 October 2026, artists are notified on 20 October, hand delivery is 30 and 31 October, and the show runs 15 November to 18 December 2026 with a reception on Sunday 15 November. The gallery takes 30% commission on sales. Shipped work goes to Fine Art Security Transport in New Britain rather than to the Association, with a $65 handling fee and prepaid shipping both ways. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: $35 + $15 each additional ($30 members). Prize: Over $1,600 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 14th Annual International Juried Print Exhibition · Remarque Print Workshop & Gallery
item.description: Remarque Print Workshop & Gallery in Albuquerque - founded in 1996 as New Grounds and, in its own words, the only non-toxic professional print workshop in the city - invites printmakers from around the world to its 14th Annual International Juried Print Exhibition, on view at the workshop's new Edith Boulevard space from 11 December 2026 to 30 January 2027. The brief asks for innovative prints drawn from all printmaking traditions, 'including, but not limited to: relief, etching, monotype, collagraph, photopolymer intaglio', and says the gallery is particularly interested in combinations of traditions. Read the gate carefully before entering, because this is a printmaking show rather than a photography show: straight and digitally output photographs are out - 'No digital images; no giclee reproductions' - but photopolymer intaglio is named in the organiser's own list of welcome processes, and that list is open-ended - 'all printmaking traditions, including, but not limited to' - so photographic intaglio work made as a print is inside the brief; Remarque's 2026 programme included an exhibition called The Printmaker and the Photographic Image: Dissolving Media Boundaries. Each artist submits three prints, original, two-dimensional and made within the last three years, on paper no larger than 16 by 20 inches. Entry is $35 through CaFE, and the show is juried and curated by the team at Remarque rather than by a named outside juror. There is no cash award: what comes back is the hang, and Remarque archivally frames every selected work at its own cost, so beyond the entry fee the artist pays only shipping in both directions and must supply a prepaid return label. All work must be for sale; the gallery retains 50% of the retail price and pays the artist within 30 days of the close. Entries must be posted by midnight MDT on 1 November 2026, the jury result comes back through CaFE by 9 November, and accepted prints must reach Remarque by 27 November. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Aesthetic Dynamics · LoosenArt
item.description: LoosenArt's open call for a new issue of its Issue Collective editorial project, on the theme Aesthetic Dynamics. Entry is free and open worldwide, and the accepted media are stated plainly: photographic, video and digital works are welcome, with no restriction on style or genre. The theme asks for contemporary readings of aesthetic dynamism, a lineage the call traces from the nineteenth-century study of the organic world — when the microscope, X-rays and microphotography opened up dimensions that had been difficult to observe — through Art Nouveau's curved, sinuous lines and fluid forms, and Futurism's speed, movement and simultaneity, to what those ways of seeing can become now. Selected works are brought together inside the publication as a single editorial narrative connecting different contemporary interpretations of the theme. A selection of the works chosen for publication will also be considered for a further selection process leading to a group exhibition to be held in 2027 in one of three cities — Milan, Rome or Cagliari — which the organiser has not yet fixed. Submission is through a Google Form asking for name, country, email, website, Instagram, an artist statement of up to 70 words in English, and up to three image files of no more than 5 MB each, renamed for the work's title. The deadline is 17 October 2026. Be aware that LoosenArt's site is now a spare Google Sites presence run from Quartu Sant'Elena in Sardinia, and beyond the call text itself it publishes no further terms; no charge of any kind is mentioned at any stage, either on the call page or in the entry form. — Deadline: October 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Curatorial Research Fellowship 2027 · Les Rencontres d'Arles
item.description: Les Rencontres d'Arles offers a curatorial research fellowship of up to €20,000, open to all exhibition curators, for an unpublished project connected to the image and to photography. It runs in two phases: a period of research around an exhibition project, and then — if the festival validates that research after six months — production of the exhibition itself. The money splits the same way. €5,000 is paid to the winner outright as an author's fee; the remaining €15,000 is conditional on validation and is a production budget steered by the Rencontres, covering loans of works, transport to Arles and back, production of the works (prints, framing, wallpapers, video and so on), the curator's invitation and, where applicable, the artists' costs in Arles during opening week or the installation, and insurance. Scenography, communication, installation, de-installation and invigilation are carried by the festival on top of that budget. In exchange the curator undertakes to select the works making up the exhibition's corpus and settle their presentation and reproduction rights, to conceive and write a presentation text for the selection of photographs, and to be present during the festival's opening week and take part in the guided tour of the exhibition. The application is a single PDF of no more than 10 MB, in the order the organiser specifies: a presentation text for the proposed exhibition project of at most 5,000 characters; the corpus of works and artists envisaged, with visuals strongly recommended; a provisional research budget of €5,000; a research schedule; a provisional production budget of €15,000; and the curator's biography, with training, full contact details and a list of the projects and exhibitions they have realised. Texts may be in French or English, ideally both. Applications opened on 16 September 2026 and close on 30 November 2026; the winning projects are announced at the end of February 2027, the research phase runs to summer 2027, and the study is delivered between September and mid-October 2027, after which production begins if the project is validated. There is no application fee. Note that this is a call for exhibition curators, not a call for photographers to submit their own pictures. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €20,000.

item.title: 2026 Architectural Photography Competition (APC26) · AIA Long Beach/South Bay
item.description: The biennial architectural photography competition of the American Institute of Architects' Long Beach/South Bay chapter, open to photographers as well as architects and designers — the chapter's own announcement invites "photographers, architects, designers, and lovers of the built environment". Entries are accepted 31 August to 31 October 2026 in three categories: Exterior (form, materials, context, light, landscape and the relationship between a building and its surroundings), Interior (composition, materiality, light, scale, detail and the experience of being within a space) and, new for 2026, Regional Focus, for architecture inside the chapter's own Long Beach/South Bay boundaries. All entries automatically qualify for a People's Choice award. Enter one category per image; multiple entries are welcome. The chapter states plainly that judging focuses on the photographic image rather than the architecture itself. No cash prize is published: winners are announced in early December 2026 and asked for a print-quality high-resolution file, and Regional Focus selections may additionally be redrawn as sketches for the 2027 Color Your City architecture coloring book with the photographer credited. In the 2024 edition the chapter published each winning photograph alongside written comments from all three jurors — Nirav Solanki, Janna Ireland and Paul Turang — plus an online gallery of every submission; the 2026 jury has not been announced on either the announcement or the entry guidelines. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $35 non-members / $25 AIA members / $10 students. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Attraction to Abstraction 2026 · Wayne Art Center
item.description: Wayne Art Center's juried exhibition of abstract work, hung in the Vidinghoff and Radnor Township Galleries outside Philadelphia alongside CraftForms, the centre's 31st International Exhibition of Contemporary Fine Craft. Photography is one of the five media named as eligible — "Painting, Works on Paper, Photography, Mixed Media and Fiber Works" — so this is one of the few regional abstraction shows where lens-based work is explicitly invited. Up to three abstract works may be entered on one application at $25 per piece; each must have been completed since January 2024, must not have been shown at Wayne Art Center before, must be at least 24 inches in each direction including any frame, and must be for sale, with the centre retaining a 40% commission. All accepted work is hand-delivered to and collected from Wayne, Pennsylvania on set dates — nothing is shipped in either direction, with no exceptions. The juror of entry is Vlad Milan Duchev, born in Pokrov, Ukraine in 1965, who trained first in painting at an art school in Bila Tserkva and then as a classical double bassist at the Music College of Zhytomyr, the Music Academy of Kharkiv and the National Conservatory of Ukraine in Kyiv, painting alongside his musical career throughout. Registration runs 22 September to 21 October 2026, notification 31 October, hand delivery 23 November, and the exhibition runs 6 December 2026 to 23 January 2027, opening the evening of 5 December at the CraftForms Preview Party. Note that the two surfaces disagree on scope: the CaFÉ prospectus opens the call to "WAC students, WAC members and regional artists 18 years of age and older" without defining the region, while wayneart.org's exhibition page describes the show as work "by our adult students and WAC community members" in a paragraph that still carries last year's title. — Deadline: October 21, 2026. Fee: $25 per work (up to 3 works). Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Signed, Sealed, Delivered: A Postcard Exhibition & Fundraiser · Albrecht-Kemper Museum of Art
item.description: A free, open postcard show at the Albrecht-Kemper Museum of Art in Saint Joseph, Missouri: artists make original 4 × 6 inch postcard artworks, up to five each, in any medium — so photographic prints, contact prints, cyanotypes and other camera-made work all qualify. Be clear about the bargain before entering: this is a fundraiser. Every postcard is exhibited and then sold for $10 with the proceeds going to the museum, the work is not returned to the artist, and there is no prize. What a photographer gets in exchange is a museum wall from late October through 3 January and a buyer who sees their name on the back — the museum asks that the artist's name go on the reverse only, with accompanying information such as a social media handle or website, so that anyone who buys a card can find more of the work. There is no entry fee and no jurying is announced. Postcards are mailed or dropped off to the museum at 2818 Frederick Avenue, Saint Joseph, MO 64506, marked ATTN: Postcard Exhibition, by 23 October 2026. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Present of Presence: Live the Moment · Cape Cod Museum of Art
item.description: The Cape Cod Museum of Art's annual members' juried exhibition, held at the museum's building on Hope Lane in Dennis, Massachusetts. The brief is about attention: in a world of relentless headlines, buzzing devices and climate anxiety, the museum asks what it means to truly inhabit this moment — to see, listen, feel, notice and connect without reaching for the next distraction. Work might celebrate a fleeting encounter, reveal something overlooked, embrace stillness, or capture the intensity of being alive in an uncertain world. Photography is named first in the museum's own list of what will be considered: photography, printmaking, textile, multi-media and three-dimensional artwork. The exhibition is open only to CCMoA members, but membership is bought at the point of entry rather than earned — the call says outright "Not yet a Member of the Cape Cod Museum of Art? You can join today to enter!", and membership runs $30 for students, $50 individual and $85 dual/family, purchasable online. It must stay current through 31 March 2027. Members may submit up to five artworks at $20 for the first and $10 for each additional one, plus a ticket service fee of $0.50 on the first entry and $0.25 on each additional one added at checkout; entry fees are non-refundable. Work must be original, new to CCMoA and not previously exhibited there; any prints must be limited edition and signed. There are no size limits — scale is decided by gallery space. Work arrives framed or on gallery-wrapped canvas at least 1.5 inches deep, ready to hang. AI-generated artwork is not accepted. Juror's Awards of $300, $200 and $100 are presented at the opening reception and gallery talk on Thursday 14 January 2027; the museum has not yet named the juror. Selected artists are notified by end of day on 17 December 2026 and the exhibition runs 8 January to 21 March 2027; work may optionally be offered for sale, on a 60/40 split in the artist's favour. Entries close at noon Eastern on Monday 14 December 2026. — Deadline: December 14, 2026. Fee: $20 first artwork, $10 each additional. Prize: $300 + Exhibition.

item.title: Devotion — Fall 2026 Online Exhibition · Analog Forever Magazine
item.description: Analog Forever Magazine's Fall 2026 online group exhibition, guest-curated by Laura Barth. The brief asks what we give ourselves to. Devotion takes many forms — sacred or secular, private or communal, quiet or consuming — and the call invites photographers to consider the people, places, practices and beliefs to which we give our attention again and again: tending gardens, caring for bodies, returning to familiar places, repeating gestures, preserving memories, making offerings, keeping vigil. The curator is explicit that devotion has shadows too, and that love can become obsession, faith fanaticism, ritual compulsion; work about the cost of loyalty is as welcome as work about its comforts. Interpretations may be spiritual, romantic, familial, ecological, creative, personal or entirely unexpected. This is an analog call — the magazine asks photographers to explore the theme through film and analog photography. Laura Barth is a lens-based multidisciplinary artist who works through experimental analog photographic processes, particularly Polaroid emulsion lifts, turning memory, spirituality and personal mythology into tactile, emotive images; her work has been shown in galleries and in print in the United States and abroad. Submissions go through a Google Form linked from the call page, and selected work goes live when the online exhibition launches on 30 November 2026. Entries close 1 November 2026. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Black Creativity Juried Art Exhibition — General Category · Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
item.description: The 57th edition of Black Creativity, the longest continually running exhibition of African American art in the United States, shown at Chicago's Griffin Museum of Science and Industry since 1970. The General Category is open to professional and emerging Black artists aged 18 and over from anywhere in the United States; a separate Teen Category serves Chicagoland artists aged 14 to 17. The museum's own exhibition page names photography outright in the media it shows, alongside paintings, drawings, fine art prints, sculpture, mixed media and ceramics, and the call's medium line reads simply 'contemporary works created in any visual medium' — video is accommodated too, on monitors the museum provides. Three jurors read the submissions: Eddie Chambers, the Goldabelle McComb Finn Distinguished Professor in Art History at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago; Monica Haslip, founder and executive director of Little Black Pearl; and D.E. Simmons, executive director of Diaspora Rhythms. Awards are $4,000 for Best in Show, $2,750 for second place and $1,500 for third, and award winners also receive two tickets to the 2027 Black Creativity Gala. Entry is $10 for up to four works completed between 2024 and 2026, and jurying is blind — you are asked to strip watermarks, credits and your own name from images and statements before uploading. Work must be original, unsold, and not previously selected for a Black Creativity exhibition; AI-generated work is excluded in those same words. Two-dimensional pieces may not exceed 84 inches in any direction and nothing may weigh more than 70 pounds; the museum cannot install ceiling-hung or projected work. Submissions close 11:59pm CST on 11 October 2026, acceptances go out by 4 November, shipping runs 1–16 December with local drop-off on 18–19 December, and the exhibition runs 18 January to 18 April 2027. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: $4,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Delfina Foundation — Portugal & Lusophone Africa Residency 2027
item.description: A twelve-week, fully funded London residency at Delfina Foundation for contemporary visual artists born in Portugal, Angola, Mozambique, Guinea-Bissau, Cape Verde or São Tomé and Príncipe, run in partnership with the UK branch of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation. The residency sits inside Delfina's 'open' summer 2027 season — independent research rather than a set theme — and runs 28 June to 17 September 2027. The package is unusually complete: a return economy flight, UK airport transfers, reimbursement of visa fees where required, a £40-a-day living allowance, a £1,200 materials budget, a London travel pass, and a single bedroom with a desk in the Delfina house, which takes up to eight residents around shared bathrooms, laundry, kitchen, library and dining room. Alongside time and space, the season's programme includes guided visits to museums, galleries, non-profits and artist-run spaces in and beyond London, organised encounters with artists, curators, academics and researchers, and professional development in the form of presentations, crits, portfolio reviews and mentoring. Applicants must be seeking to develop their practice through research, be able to explain how an international residency would serve their career and local networks, and be confident discussing their work in English, since the interview is held in English. Artists currently based in the UK are not eligible. The application is a Cognito form asking for a CV and either a portfolio PDF or a personal website, with your practice described in five keywords and again in fifty words, plus contact details for two professional referees. Duos and collectives are discouraged by the accommodation — Delfina asks that one member represent the group — and the foundation states plainly that it welcomes D/deaf, disabled and neurodivergent applicants and will discuss adapting the residency to access needs. Previous unsuccessful applicants are explicitly encouraged to apply again. Applications close 23:59 BST on Sunday 4 October 2026 and everyone is notified by mid-November. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Funded residency + £1,200 materials budget.

item.title: In Practice: Annual Juried Exhibition · Foothills Art Center
item.description: Foothills Art Center in Golden, Colorado has run an annual Members' Exhibition for over a decade; this year it is renamed In Practice and, for the first time, membership is no longer required to apply. The centre frames the change around its own argument: there is a place for theory, but exhibiting is where artistic technique and decisions are tested in practice, and an artist's practice is never finished or stagnant. All media are eligible, including alternative media — the organiser's phrasing, with no exclusions attached — and work must be original, not previously shown at Foothills, and ready to hang or install. There is no size restriction, though larger works are assessed on whether they use scale effectively. You may enter up to three works and a maximum of one will be selected.
